fig1_change_of_variables.svg: Transforming X ~ U(0,1) by Y = -ln(X). The change-of-variables density f_Y(y) = f_X(g^{-1}(y)) |dx/dy| (orange) lands exactly on the Exp(1) target (dashed) and on a histogram of transformed samples, confirming the Jacobian formula.
fig2_convolution_sum.svg: The density of a sum of independent variables is the convolution of their densities. For two Uniform(0,1) terms the convolution integral (orange) gives the triangular law on [0,2] (dashed closed form), matching a histogram of sampled sums.
